title: The surface must not offer a goal.close the command path will refuse: gate the offer on the bootstrap prerequisite too
description:
Spun out of task-8fdd81b81c0f4dc88c16203de139e2ba (SPIDR child 3 of task-d1c815eb) by worker-56ac23da 2026-09-05. That row owns the browser end of goal closure and is FORBIDDEN by its own task rail 1 from making a daemon change, so the defect it measured is filed here.

MEASURED ON THE LIVE UnAI LOOP, not inferred. Full transcript in comment-41108de3b6b44efc844fec78a522bcee on task-8fdd81b8. Shipped daemon on D:/projexts/UnAI/.moe-next/store.sqlite (MOE_PROJECT_ID=unai), real built control-room bundle, real chromium, operator-stdin pairing.

THE DEFECT. ONE `/affordances/read` frame contains BOTH of these, at the same instant:
  steps[]  -> { "kind": "goal.close", "status": "BLOCKED", ... }
  nextAllowedCommands[] -> { "commandKind": "goal.close", "targetAggregateId": "goal-c9d9850b-ccef-4c14-8893-a162e3aaf679", "expectedVersion": 2, ... }
The daemon's own step projection says the command is BLOCKED while its offer roster hands the browser a live affordance for it. The control room does exactly what it should with an offer — Needs you rendered "Ready to close ... Close the goal" for two goals — and the click then fails.

WHAT THE OPERATOR GETS. Dispatching that exact offer answers, in 212 ms:
  {"httpStatus":422,"ok":false,"outcome":"PORT_REFUSED","refusal":{"code":"BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING","detail":"BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING","httpStatus":422,"layer":"DAEMON_PREREQUISITE"},"stage":"DISPATCH"}
Not one of the nine GOAL_PREREQUISITE_REFUSAL_CODES. A generic bootstrap code that names nothing about goals, criteria or closure, on a goal whose criteria are 10/10 VERIFIED and whose contract is APPROVED. An operator cannot act on it.

ROOT CAUSE, symbol by symbol.
- `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts:22` — `"goal.close": Object.freeze(["approval.decide"])`.
- `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-services.ts:257-260` — `missingPrerequisites(ledger, request.kind)` refuses BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING @ DAEMON_PREREQUISITE BEFORE any goal handler runs.
- `apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-planning-offers.ts:170-178` — the offer gate consults ONLY `input.closeReadiness(goal.goalId)` (child 2 task-8145137c's criteria gate) and never `missingPrerequisites`. So the two authorities disagree by construction.
- On the `unai` project `approval.decide` has COMMITTED=0 (status READY): its goals were activated through the browser's `approval.decide_intent` path. The prerequisite is project-wide, so NO goal on such a project can ever close, while every n/n-verified goal on it is still offered a Close.

WHY THIS IS THE HIGH-VALUE FIX. It is the "dead button" hazard the parent's plan named as its biggest risk, shipped and reachable. It also makes the live product's headline journey — close a finished goal from the browser — unreachable end to end on any project approved via approval.decide_intent, which is the browser's only approval path.

SCOPE. Daemon only. Do NOT relax the command-path gate: the offer must stop being made, not the refusal stop being raised. Suggested shape (architect to measure and decide): widen `PlanningOfferInput` with the same `missingPrerequisites` read the command path uses and withhold `goal.close` (and, for the same reason, check `repository.publish`, which shares the `approval.decide` prerequisite and shows the identical BLOCKED-step-with-live-offer split in the same frame). If the deeper answer is that `approval.decide_intent` should satisfy the `goal.close` prerequisite, that is a sequence-table change and needs its own measurement — either way one authority must decide, not two.

REPRODUCTION that needs no live store: any project whose approval went through approval.decide_intent. The parent row's recorded frames are committed at apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-close-frames.fixture.ts.
definitionOfDone: A daemon test proves the two authorities agree: for a goal whose project has NO committed approval.decide, /affordances/read emits NO goal.close entry in nextAllowedCommands — asserted on the same frame that carries steps[goal.close].status === 'BLOCKED', so the arm fails if the split ever reopens.

The converse arm: for a goal whose project HAS a committed approval.decide and whose closeReadiness is READY or NO_CONTRACT, the offer is still made — the fix withholds only what the command path would refuse and does not regress child 2 (task-8145137ca3c144f0878deb83d05bab63) or child 1 (task-ae6fd9aca46c42d8af940ff6f336afbb).

The command-path gate is UNCHANGED: bootstrap-services.ts still answers BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING for a direct dispatch that skips the surface, pinned by an arm that dispatches without an offer. Fail-closed is preserved; only the offer is withheld.

repository.publish is measured the same way and either fixed with goal.close or explicitly recorded as out of scope with the measurement quoted — it shares the approval.decide prerequisite and shows the same BLOCKED-step-with-live-offer split in the recorded frame.
Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Note `pnpm test` covers no apps/** and is not evidence.
taskRails: THE OFFER IS WRONG, NOT THE REFUSAL. Never relax bootstrap-services.ts:257-260 or the GOAL_PREREQUISITE codes to make a close succeed. The command path staying fail-closed is the invariant; the surface must stop advertising what it will refuse.

Re-measure before planning: the parent measured this at 2026-09-05 on branch moe/work-2026-09-04. Re-run `grep -n 'goal.close' apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts` and `sed -n '170,178p' apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-planning-offers.ts` before writing a plan against them.

implementationPlan.description:
READ THE OWNER DECISION FIRST, THEN RE-MEASURE. Read comment-5a8278d76aa24b44989a906caaef589b (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05) in full before anything else. It carries an OWNER DECISION taken in the planning REPL that SUPERSEDES this row's title and its DoD 1 and DoD 3. The row is titled "gate the offer"; the ruling is the opposite — do NOT withhold the offer, FIX THE PREREQUISITE, because a goal approved in the browser commits no `approval.decide` and would otherwise be permanently uncloseable. Withholding the offer would ship a dead end: honest, and unfixable by any operator action. If you plan to do anything that withholds an offer, stop and re-read.

Task rail 2 requires re-measurement before planning against these lines. Run them and print the output:
  (a) `grep -n 'goal.close\|repository.publish' apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts` — expect :22 `"goal.close": Object.freeze(["approval.decide"])` and :25 the same for `repository.publish`. BOTH name the same prerequisite, which is why ONE table entry fixes both (amended DoD 4).
  (b) `sed -n '62,85p' apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts` — the `PREREQUISITE_ALTERNATIVES` table and `unmetPrerequisites`. This is the seam the fix uses; it already exists for `goal.create_with_source` and its docblock explains why it is a SEPARATE table (keeping `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES` byte-identical for two consumers that cast and iterate it).
  (c) `sed -n '95,112p' apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-ledger.ts` — `readDurableLedger`. Confirm `kinds` is `new Set<string>()` filled by `kinds.add(decision.commandKind)` for EVERY committed decision, not only bootstrap kinds. This is what makes the fix work at all.
  (d) `grep -n 'approval.decide_intent' apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts` — expect :366 `ledger.kinds.has("approval.decide") || ledger.kinds.has("approval.decide_intent")`. That is the PRODUCTION PRECEDENT: this exact widening already ships one layer up, for the same reason, on the same ledger set.

TWO REDS ARE PREDICTED AT PLAN TIME. Confirm both before you fix anything, so you know your arms are real:
  1. `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-durability.test.ts:615-635` ("names only real command kinds on both sides of the alternatives table") checks every alternative against `BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS`. `approval.decide_intent` is NOT a bootstrap kind, so this arm goes RED the moment the entry is added. Step 4 corrects it deliberately — do not delete it and do not discover it mid-step.
  2. The table's value type is `readonly BootstrapCommandKind[]`, so the new entry will not typecheck until the type is widened. Step 3 handles it.

Note peer dirt and continue: the checkout is shared and had foreign dirty paths at plan time. Never revert, stash or `git add -A`.

RED ARMS FIRST, at the durable level, in apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-durability.test.ts. Copy the shape of the arm that already exists at :563 ("accepts plan.propose after goal.create_with_source, with no goal.create in the ledger") — it is the precedent for exactly this kind of alternative and it drives real commands against a real store rather than asserting on the table.

Write these and watch them FAIL before the fix:
  1. ACCEPTS AFTER decide_intent (amended DoD 1'). Drive a world to an approved goal via `approval.decide_intent`, with NO `approval.decide` in the ledger, then dispatch `goal.close`. It must be ACCEPTED. Assert the durable outcome, not merely the absence of a throw.
  2. THE SAME FOR repository.publish (amended DoD 4). Same world, dispatch `repository.publish`. Accepted. Both kinds share the `approval.decide` prerequisite line, so this arm is what proves the single entry covered both rather than only the one you were looking at.
  3. STILL FAILS CLOSED WITH NEITHER (amended DoD 3'). A world with NEITHER `approval.decide` NOR `approval.decide_intent` committed dispatches `goal.close` and must still refuse with code exactly `BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING` at layer exactly `DAEMON_PREREQUISITE` (bootstrap-services.ts:292-295). Assert BOTH the code and the layer — global rail 1 — and assert no decision was committed on that path. This is the arm proving the gate was CORRECTED, not REMOVED, and it is the one QA will look for hardest.
  4. THE REPORTED MISSING KIND STAYS THE PRIMARY. On the world from arm 3, assert `missingPrerequisites(readDurableLedger(store, PROJECT_ID), "goal.close")` equals `["approval.decide"]` — the PRIMARY kind, never the alternative. The arm at :611 does exactly this for `plan.propose`; the docblock at :53-56 explains why it matters (the control room parses `missing` as plain strings at live/live-board-feed.ts:118-127, and a leaked group literal would take the board's BLOCKED card dark).

Assert against the production surface throughout. Do not write a local helper that re-derives prerequisite resolution.

THE FIX — two edits in apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts, and nothing else in this step.

(1) WIDEN THE ALTERNATIVES VALUE TYPE. `PREREQUISITE_ALTERNATIVES` (:62-66) is typed `Readonly<Partial<Record<BootstrapCommandKind, readonly BootstrapCommandKind[]>>>`. The VALUE type must become `readonly string[]` (the key type stays `BootstrapCommandKind` — `approval.decide` is one, at :19). This is safe and the reason is measurable: the alternative is only ever tested with `committed.has(alternative)` at :83, and `unmetPrerequisites` takes `committed: ReadonlySet<string>` while `readDurableLedger` builds `kinds` as `new Set<string>()` over EVERY committed decision kind. The function's RETURN type is unchanged — it filters `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES[kind]`, whose entries are still `BootstrapCommandKind`, so the "missing names the PRIMARY" guarantee the docblock makes is untouched.

(2) ADD ONE ENTRY:
    "approval.decide": Object.freeze(["approval.decide_intent"] as const),
ONE entry fixes BOTH `goal.close` (:22) and `repository.publish` (:25) because both name `approval.decide` as their prerequisite. Do not add a second entry per kind.

EXTEND THE DOCBLOCK at :41-60 in the file's existing voice, and make it carry the WHY, because the next reader's instinct will be to "tidy" this away. It must say: the browser's paired session approves through `approval.decide_intent` (the daemon-owned approval seam), so a goal approved in the browser never commits an `approval.decide` and its `goal.close` / `repository.publish` prerequisite would otherwise be UNSATISFIABLE FOREVER — measured live on UnAI, a goal at 10/10 criteria VERIFIED refusing BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING. Say that `affordance-read.ts:366` already accepts either approval kind off this same `ledger.kinds` set, so this entry makes the prerequisite agree with a rule the read surface has enforced for longer. Keep the existing sentence that widening is always explicit and always one named kind, and keep the fail-closed sentence — both are still true.

DO NOT TOUCH `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES`. Its entries stay byte-identical; that is the whole reason the alternatives table exists (docblock :49-56), and two suites this row does not own cast and iterate it. Do NOT relax bootstrap-services.ts:292-295 or any GOAL_PREREQUISITE code — task rail 1 is unchanged by the owner decision: the command path staying fail-closed is the invariant, and what changes is only WHICH committed kinds satisfy the requirement.

Arms 1, 2 and 4 from step 2 should now be GREEN, and arm 3 should still be green. The alternatives sweep should now be RED — that is step 4.

CORRECT THE ALTERNATIVES SWEEP — the predicted red, in apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-durability.test.ts:615-635 ("names only real command kinds on both sides of the alternatives table").

Why it reds: it sets `const roster: readonly string[] = BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS` and then asserts BOTH sides of every entry are in that roster. `approval.decide_intent` is served by the runtime registry and is NOT a bootstrap kind, so the ALTERNATIVE side fails.

The arm is a REAL guard with a stated rationale — "a kind no dispatch serves could never appear in a committed set" — so CORRECT it, do not delete it and do not weaken it to a subset check. The rationale is right; the roster it measures against was too narrow. Fix the roster, keep the property:
  - The PREREQUISITE (key) side keeps checking `BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS`: a prerequisite is always a bootstrap kind, since the keys come from `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES`. Do not widen this side — widening it would let a non-bootstrap key in and lose a real check.
  - The ALTERNATIVE side checks `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` (imported from `@moe/contracts`), which is the honest roster of kinds that CAN appear in a committed set. Verified at plan time: `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` contains `approval.decide_intent`, and `BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS` is declared `as const satisfies readonly RuntimeCommandKind[]` (bootstrap-contracts.ts:43), so bootstrap kinds remain a strict subset and nothing already passing starts failing.
  - Keep BOTH zero-yield guards exactly as they are: `expect(entries.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` and `expect(checked).toBeGreaterThan(0)`. A sweep that generates zero checks passes while testing nothing, and the entry count is about to change from 1 to 2.
  - Update the arm's comment to say why the two sides now measure against DIFFERENT rosters — otherwise it reads as an inconsistency and the next reader "fixes" it back.

DEPENDENCY EDGE, already proven — no manifest work: `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts:1` imports `JsonObject` from the bare specifier `@moe/contracts` and `bootstrap-contracts.ts` imports `RuntimeCommandKind` from it, both compiling today. Confirm the import resolves and move on.

THE TWO AUTHORITIES AGREE ON ONE FRAME — amended DoD 1', in apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.test.ts.

The original DoD 1 asked for a frame carrying NO `goal.close` offer. Under the owner decision the requirement INVERTS: for a goal approved via `approval.decide_intent` whose criteria are ready, `/affordances/read` OFFERS `goal.close` AND the command path ACCEPTS it. Assert both against the SAME world, so the arm fails if the two authorities ever diverge again — that split, offer-live-while-step-BLOCKED, is the whole defect.

Build a world whose ledger has `approval.decide_intent` committed and no `approval.decide`, with a goal whose closeReadiness is READY. Then assert, in one arm:
  (a) the frame's `nextAllowedCommands` CONTAINS a `goal.close` entry for that goal;
  (b) the frame's `steps[]` entry for `goal.close` is NOT `BLOCKED` — the projection and the offer roster now say the same thing;
  (c) dispatching that exact offer (its `commandId`, `expectedVersion` and `targetAggregateId`, taken from the frame rather than invented) is ACCEPTED.
Taking the dispatch parameters FROM THE FRAME is what makes this an agreement test rather than two independent assertions that could both be right about different worlds.

The offer gate at `apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-planning-offers.ts` needs NO change — measured at plan time: it consults `closeReadiness`, and the prerequisite is what was wrong. If you find yourself editing that file, stop: either the measurement moved or you are re-implementing the withhold the owner decision rejected. Report rather than proceeding.

If a suitable world builder does not already exist in this suite, extend the nearest one rather than writing a parallel fixture that re-derives ledger state — a frame assembled by a helper that reimplements the production reader proves nothing about production.

GATES. Run each STANDALONE and in the FOREGROUND — no pipe, no `;` chain, no `&&` (a piped run reports tail's exit code; a chain reports only the last command's):
  1. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`
  2. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`
  3. `pnpm typecheck`

READ THE OUTPUT, NOT THE EXIT CODE. `pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0 when the filter misses; "No test files found" and "0 passed" are also exit 0. The discriminator is the `Test Files N passed` count line with N nonzero — quote it for all three legs. DoD 5 says it explicitly: `pnpm test` covers no `apps/**` and is NOT evidence for anything in this row.

Name `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` as the complete_task verification command.

The daemon suite is SLOW (~22 min) and FLAKY — two back-to-back baselines on this branch gave `17 failed | 416 passed` then `10 failed | 423 passed`, dominated by 30000ms timeouts from the spawn-latency cliff. So a whole-suite pass/fail delta is NOT admissible attribution. Attribute by PATH per global rail 3: record repo-wide failures at the merge-base, then at HEAD, subtract, and intersect with this row's three owned paths. This row touches exactly three files, all under apps/daemon, so `git diff --name-only` is itself most of the attribution proof — say that plainly. Report any foreign red verbatim with its exact failing lines and file paths: disclosed, never hidden, never fabricated green.

Run the targeted files first for a fast signal before committing to the full suite: the two bootstrap suites and the affordance-read suite.

DRILLS AND ADVERSARIAL PASS.

DRILL 1, THE ONE THAT MATTERS. Remove the new `"approval.decide"` entry from `PREREQUISITE_ALTERNATIVES` and re-run the targeted arms. Step 2's arms 1 and 2 (accepts `goal.close` and `repository.publish` after `decide_intent`) MUST both go RED. If only one reds, the single-entry-covers-both claim is unproven and one of the two kinds is being satisfied by something else — find out what before proceeding.

DRILL 2, FAIL-CLOSED IS REAL. Add a SECOND alternative that should not satisfy anything — e.g. map `approval.decide` to a kind the world never commits — and confirm step 2's arm 3 (neither approval kind → BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE) still refuses. The widening must admit exactly one named act and nothing else.

DRILL 3, THE SWEEP STILL BITES. Add an alternative that is in NEITHER roster (a made-up kind). The corrected sweep from step 4 must go RED. If it stays green, the roster widening went too far and the guard is now decorative.

RESTORE PROOF, global rail 13. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths BEFORE drilling. All three files in this row are TRACKED, so an empty `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof for each — run it per path and quote it. (If you created any new file, that path is UNTRACKED and `git diff` is blind to it: back it up out of tree, suffixed with your worker id, and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore.)

THEN ASK, answering each in the completion record:
  - Does any OTHER kind depend on `approval.decide` as a prerequisite that this widening now also affects? `grep -n 'approval.decide' apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts` — at plan time exactly `goal.close` (:22) and `repository.publish` (:25). If a third appeared, say so; it is in scope by construction and must be asserted, not silently widened.
  - Is there any path where a REJECTED `approval.decide_intent` commits a decision that would now satisfy the prerequisite? `approval-intent-rejection.ts` holds the durable REJECT half. A rejected approval must NOT enable a close. Measure it and state the answer — if a reject does commit under the same kind, that is a real hole and this row must close it or report it, not leave it unmeasured.
  - Concurrency: two operators closing the same goal at once — the expectedVersion fence answers, and no arm should assert merely "threw".

COMPLETION RECORD states: that the ruling followed comment-5a8278d76aa24b44989a906caaef589b's owner decision and why the row's TITLE is not what shipped (the offer was not withheld; the prerequisite was corrected); that `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES` is byte-identical; that one entry covered both `goal.close` and `repository.publish` with both asserted; that the alternatives sweep was corrected rather than deleted, with the two-roster reason; and the drill outcomes with their restore proofs.

comments.content:
ROOT CAUSE IS DEEPER THAN THIS ROW'S TITLE, and the fix changes (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05, owner decision taken in the planning REPL).

WHAT THE FILER MEASURED IS REAL AND I REPRODUCED THE MECHANISM. But "gate the offer on the bootstrap prerequisite too" treats the SYMPTOM. Measured at HEAD:

  apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts:18-25
    "goal.close":         Object.freeze(["approval.decide"]),
    "repository.publish": Object.freeze(["approval.decide"]),

  apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts:175-176 accepts EITHER approval kind:
    entry.commandKind === "approval.decide" || entry.commandKind === "approval.decide_intent"

The browser's PAIRED SESSION approves through `approval.decide_intent` (mint + activation, task-6093483c) - affordance-read.ts's own comment at :341-345 records that a goal enabled that way "must surface its code nodes exactly as the seeded approval.decide journey always has", and notes the first real project's approved goal sat EXECUTION_ENABLED with zero node.deliver steps behind exactly this gate.

SO: a goal approved IN THE BROWSER never commits an `approval.decide`. Its prerequisite for `goal.close` and `repository.publish` is therefore UNSATISFIABLE FOREVER. That is why the live UnAI goal sits at 10/10 criteria VERIFIED and refuses BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING - not because the offer was premature, but because the command path does not recognise how the goal was approved.

WITHHOLDING THE OFFER WOULD SHIP A DEAD END. The button would stop lying, and the goal would still be permanently uncloseable and unpublishable. The operator would be told, honestly, that there is nothing they can do - which is worse than the current bug in the one way that matters: the current bug is fixable by a click that fails, the withheld version is fixable by nothing.

OWNER DECISION: make `approval.decide_intent` SATISFY the prerequisite for `goal.close` and `repository.publish`, so both authorities agree at the cause. Fail-closed is preserved - a goal with NEITHER approval kind still refuses. The accepted set widens by exactly one equivalent human act, the one the browser actually performs.

AMENDED SCOPE (supersedes DoD 1 and DoD 3 as written):
- DoD 1' : the two authorities agree because the PREREQUISITE now accepts either approval kind. For a goal approved via decide_intent, /affordances/read offers goal.close AND the command path ACCEPTS it - assert the dispatch succeeds, on the same frame that carries the offer. For a goal with NEITHER approval kind, no offer and a refusal.
- DoD 3' : the command-path gate is not REMOVED, it is CORRECTED. bootstrap-services.ts:259 still answers BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING for a goal whose project has neither approval kind committed - pinned by an arm that dispatches without any approval. What changes is which committed kinds satisfy the requirement, not whether it is enforced.
- DoD 4 stands and gets easier: repository.publish shares the identical prerequisite line (bootstrap-sequence.ts:25), so the same fix covers it - do BOTH in this row and assert both, rather than recording publish as out of scope.

QA: grade DoD 1' and 3'. A plan that only withholds the offer leaves the UnAI goals unreachable and does not discharge this row.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
WITHHOLD THE OFFER (the row's own title) — REJECTED by owner decision, and the reasoning holds up: it makes the button stop lying while leaving every browser-approved goal permanently uncloseable and unpublishable. The current bug is fixable by a click that fails; the withheld version is fixable by nothing.

EDIT COMMAND_PREREQUISITES DIRECTLY (change `"goal.close": ["approval.decide"]` to accept either) — REJECTED. It changes that map's value type, which bootstrap-sequence.ts's own docblock records as breaking two suites this row does not own (measured TS2352 and TS2345). The alternatives table exists precisely to avoid this, and using it also keeps this row's diff off a file another row is queued to change.

WIDEN THE ALTERNATIVES SWEEP TO A SUBSET CHECK, or delete it — REJECTED. Its rationale ("a kind no dispatch serves could never appear in a committed set") is correct; only its roster was too narrow. Weakening it to make the fix pass would retire a real guard to fit the code, which is the failure mode this board's rails exist to stop. The two sides legitimately measure different rosters and the plan makes the arm say so.

SPLIT goal.close AND repository.publish INTO TWO ROWS — REJECTED. They share one prerequisite line, so one table entry fixes both; splitting would create two rows contending for one file to land two halves of a two-line change. Amended DoD 4 asks for both here.

WHERE THE AGREEMENT ARM LIVES. Asserting DoD 1' at the bootstrap level alone would prove the dispatch is accepted but not that the frame still OFFERS it, and the defect is precisely the two authorities disagreeing. So the agreement arm goes in affordance-read.test.ts and takes its dispatch parameters FROM the frame it just asserted on.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED 2026-09-05 by architect-aa54e231 on branch moe/work-2026-09-04, per task rail 2.

THE ROW'S TITLE IS NOT WHAT SHIPS. comment-5a8278d76aa24b44989a906caaef589b (architect-20a6d1eb) carries an OWNER DECISION taken in the planning REPL that supersedes DoD 1 and DoD 3: do NOT withhold the offer, correct the PREREQUISITE. Reason, and it is sound: the browser's paired session approves through `approval.decide_intent`, so a goal approved in the browser never commits an `approval.decide` and its `goal.close` prerequisite is unsatisfiable forever. Withholding the offer would replace a button that fails with a goal nothing can ever close. I plan against the amended scope; DoD 1' and 3' from that comment are the gradeable text.

THE SEAM ALREADY EXISTS AND FITS EXACTLY. `PREREQUISITE_ALTERNATIVES` (bootstrap-sequence.ts:62-66) is a SECOND table of "kinds whose own committed decision ALSO satisfies the keyed prerequisite", already carrying `goal.create -> goal.create_with_source`. `unmetPrerequisites` (:75-85) consults it. Its docblock (:49-56) records WHY it is separate: nesting alternatives inside COMMAND_PREREQUISITES changes that map's value type, which two suites this row does not own read — `daemon-command-registry.test.ts:1071` casts the whole map and `demo-seed-plan.test.ts:56` iterates an entry as flat kinds (measured TS2352/TS2345). So the fix leaves COMMAND_PREREQUISITES byte-identical, which ALSO keeps it clear of the concurrent mover on that file (see risks).
